files.evidence: Read in full (95 lines). Both exported traversals cap depth and detect cycles (13-51, 63-94) and only call injected db.getById. They do not call safeUuid as required for any LanceDB ID, but repository search found no runtime caller outside tests; without a reachable user-facing source or direct query construction in this module, the policy gap is not promoted.

Read in full (274 lines). It is pure deterministic text analysis with no file/query/process/network sink. It preserves ordering when detecting role reversal (182-200, 219-243) and requires salient terms from both inputs in merged text (246-274). False positives/negatives can cause memory-quality or merge-safety defects, but the destructive sequencing defect lives in index.js and is covered by the bug audit.

Read in full (69 lines). Pure ranking helpers use version, active status, authoritative update source, and timestamp, with deterministic tie behavior. No untrusted syntax or privileged sink exists here.

Read in full (380 lines). Recall text is analyzed in memory; topic extraction strips non-word characters and selects at most three tokens (24-40). Written Neo candidates use fixed statements or those bounded tokens and remain status=candidate (124-229), not activated instructions. Quadratic duplicate analysis at 60-75 is a performance concern, but caller recall sets are bounded and no independent attacker-controlled high-impact sink was found.

Read in full (88 lines). It is an in-memory batching helper and delegates filesystem behavior to flushFn. Failed entries are removed before the flush and never restored (62-75), and timer/onError catches silently swallow errors (28-31, 67-74), both confirmed reliability/observability defects under the repository standards. Metrics loss is not a privilege or confidentiality boundary.

notes: No security candidates. Bug audit should retain destructive merge ordering and metrics-loss/error-swallowing findings; memory-history validation is a dormant API hardening gap.
